title: The Home page, next version — the questions before anything is drawn

steps.headline: What goes inside the card that folds open and shut?
steps.today: Each room is one long card: a big tile for every light, then speakers, TV, thermostat and cameras. Every brightness bar is always showing.
steps.problem: A room with six lights fills the screen, so the room you want is a long scroll away.
steps.proposal: A folded card shows one line per room. Open it to see each light and its brightness bar.

options.label: Only the lights fold
options.summary: Each room keeps its TV, speaker and thermostat in view; just the lights are grouped into a card that folds.
pros: TV and thermostat stay one tap away.
The fold matches what the All button controls: lights.
cons: A room with a TV and a speaker is still several tiles tall when folded.

options.label: The whole room folds
options.summary: Folded, a room is one line: its name, how many lights are on, the All button. Open it to see everything in it.
pros: Shortest page: ten rooms fit on one screen.
Clearest overview of the house.
cons: Turning the TV down takes two taps instead of one.
The All button would sit beside things it does not control.

steps.path: Pages → Home, the top of a room's lights
steps.headline: What should the button that switches all of a room's lights look like?
steps.today: Each room has a text button reading All on or All off. It flips depending on whether any light is on, and it never touches TVs or speakers.
steps.problem: It looks different from the light tiles beside it, and it disappears when the room has only one light.
steps.proposal: Pick the look. Whichever you pick, it only ever controls lights.

options.label: A bulb tile with "All" under it
options.summary: The same glowing bulb as a single light, labelled All, lit when any light in the room is on. Press to flip.
pros: Looks and works exactly like the lights it controls.
Glows from across the room: easy to see a room is on while folded.
cons: Could be mistaken for a light named "All" at a glance.

options.label: The bulb tile plus one brightness bar for the room
options.summary: As above, plus a bar that dims every light in the room together.
pros: Dim a whole room without opening it.
cons: Lights at different brightness all jump to the same level when you drag it.
More to fit in a folded card.

options.label: Keep the All on / All off text button
pros: Already built and approved.
The words say exactly what it does.
cons: Does not match the tiles; you said it could look better.

steps.headline: Which rooms are open when you open the page?
steps.today: Nothing folds yet, so everything is always open.
steps.problem: Folding is only useful if the page opens the way you want it most often.
steps.proposal: The page remembers which rooms you left open, on this computer.

options.label: As you left them
pros: Your own room can stay open forever, the rest folded.
cons: A room you opened once stays open until you close it.

options.label: All folded, every time
pros: Always the same short overview.
cons: Adjusting a brightness always takes an extra tap.

options.label: Rooms with something on are open
pros: Shows what is running right now.
cons: Rooms jump open and shut as others in the house switch things, which moves what you were about to press.

steps.path: Pages → Home, a Google TV tile
steps.headline: How much control should the Google TV tiles have?
steps.today: A TV tile switches the TV on and off and sets volume. Home Assistant reaches your Google TVs only as Chromecasts, which cannot press buttons on the TV.
steps.problem: No way to pause, go back, go home, or open YouTube or Netflix from the page.
steps.proposal: Add Home Assistant's Android TV Remote connection, which acts like the TV's real remote. I set it up; you read a short code off each TV screen once.

options.label: A full remote
options.summary: Tap a TV to open a remote: arrows, OK, back, home, play/pause, volume, and buttons for your apps (YouTube, Netflix…).
pros: Everything the physical remote does, from the computer.
Works for any app on the TV, not just ones that support casting.
cons: One pairing per TV: walk to each TV and type the code it shows.
Typing on the TV with the keyboard is a later step, not this one.

options.label: Playback buttons only
options.summary: Play/pause, skip and what's playing on the tile; no arrows or app buttons.
pros: No pairing needed: works today through the Chromecast connection.
cons: Only works while something is playing; can't open an app or navigate menus.

options.label: Leave TVs as they are
pros: Nothing to set up.
cons: You still need the physical remote for everything but power and volume.

steps.headline: Which basic settings should be built into the page?
steps.today: To rename a light, move it to another room or hide one, you open Home Assistant's own screens.
steps.problem: The everyday tidying a smart home needs means leaving the page.
steps.proposal: An Edit button puts the page in edit mode: every tile shows its own small settings. Pick everything it should cover. I'd pick rename, move and reorder.

options.label: Rename a device
pros: Fixes names like "Hue color lamp 3".
cons: See the next question: whether names change only here or in Home Assistant too.

options.label: Move a device to another room, or make a new room
pros: What you just asked me to do for the bathroom speaker, done yourself.
cons: Changes Home Assistant, so it affects its app and voice assistants too.

options.label: Reorder rooms and devices
options.summary: Drag rooms and tiles into the order you want.
pros: Your room first, the guest room last.
cons: Dragging is fiddly on a small screen; arrow buttons would be offered too.

options.label: Favourites row at the top
options.summary: Star any device to put it in a row above the rooms.
pros: The three things you touch daily, never folded away.
cons: The same device then appears twice on the page.

options.label: Change a device's icon
pros: A lamp can look like a lamp, a strip like a strip.
cons: A picker to build; the least useful of these.

steps.headline: When you rename or move a device, where does the change happen?
steps.today: The page can only read and switch devices. The connection it uses cannot change Home Assistant's settings.
steps.problem: Renaming in Home Assistant itself needs a second kind of connection to it, a live one, which pages do not have yet. That is new work in the app and new wording on the approval card.
steps.proposal: Order, favourites and hiding are saved by the page; names and rooms are changed in Home Assistant itself.

options.label: Names and rooms in Home Assistant; order and favourites in the page
pros: A rename shows everywhere: the page, Home Assistant's app, voice commands.
Layout choices stay personal to this page.
cons: Needs the live connection built into the app first; the biggest piece of this round.
A page you approve could then change Home Assistant's settings, so the approval card must say so.

options.label: Everything saved only in the page
pros: No new app work: buildable right away.
Nothing the page does can change Home Assistant's setup.
cons: Names differ between the page and Home Assistant's app, and voice commands use the old names.
A move is only a move on this page.

steps.path: Pages → Home, anything the page does not cover
steps.headline: How should the page handle settings it does not have?
steps.today: There is an Open Home Assistant button on the key step only.
steps.problem: Automations, adding new devices and integrations will always live in Home Assistant. You asked whether its menus could appear inside the app, restyled.
steps.proposal: Every tile and room gets an Open in Home Assistant link to that exact device's page there.

options.label: Links to the exact screen in Home Assistant
options.summary: Opens in your browser, already on that device's settings.
pros: Small to build; never goes out of date when Home Assistant updates.
cons: You leave the app and see Home Assistant's own look.

options.label: Home Assistant's own screens inside the app
options.summary: Its real menus shown in a panel, with our colours applied on top.
pros: Every Home Assistant setting without leaving the app.
cons: Pages are deliberately blocked from showing other sites; this needs its own new built-in viewer.
Restyling another app's screens breaks whenever Home Assistant updates, often weekly.
It still asks you to log in to Home Assistant inside it.

options.label: Rebuild more menus in the page
options.summary: Recreate chosen screens, such as automations on/off, in the page's own style.
pros: Looks like the rest of the page.
cons: Each menu is new work; only worth it for the few you use a lot.

steps.headline: Which everyday features should the page add?
steps.today: Lights, thermostat, speakers, TVs and camera pictures, by room.
steps.problem: Smart home apps usually offer a few more conveniences that the page lacks.
steps.proposal: Pick everything you want in this round. Anything left out can come later. I'd pick Everything off and the status line.

options.label: Everything off
options.summary: One button at the top that switches off every light in the house.
pros: Bedtime or leaving, in one press.
cons: Easy to press by accident; it would ask first.

options.label: A status line at the top
options.summary: "5 lights on · 72° inside · front door camera clear".
pros: The house at a glance with every room folded.
cons: One more line of space.

options.label: Scenes and routines
options.summary: One-tap buttons for your Hue scenes and Home Assistant scripts.
pros: Movie mode or dinner lighting without touching each light.
cons: Hue scenes you never use show up too, so they'd need hiding.

options.label: Sensors
options.summary: Temperatures, motion, doors and batteries shown in their rooms.
pros: See which sensor has a low battery.
cons: Home Assistant lists many sensors nobody looks at; most would start hidden.

options.label: Automations on/off
options.summary: A list of your automations, each with a switch to pause it.
pros: Stop the evening lights turning on while you're away, without opening Home Assistant.
cons: Few automations exist yet.

options.label: Search
options.summary: Type a device's name to jump to it.
pros: Fast once there are many devices.
cons: With folded rooms and favourites, rarely needed.

steps.headline: This is built in rounds: folding rooms first, then TV remotes, then edit mode, each shown to you before the next.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: each round gets its own pictures to approve before code, like the last three rounds of the Home page.
steps.notice: You can keep using and testing the page between rounds; nothing half-built is installed.
